newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS TUESDAY LARGELY FIRMER.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS TUESDAY LARGELY FIRMER.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar was quoted firmer against the key U.S. dollar at the close of Tuesday's interbank market and dealers said the currency seemed on the way to recovery after the turbulence of the past week.

"The market was relatively stable today and everybody was trying by all means to come back to the one-point (bid/offer) spread. There's quite a bit of confidence renewal in the market," one dealer commented.

The drift towards stability follows the local dollar's recent free-fall stretching over a week, which was triggered by a couple of heavy import payments coupled with a statement by the central bank governor that the unit was overvalued.
During that period, some dealers were quoting as wide as 20 points to protect their foreign currency reserves and the dollar lost over 10 cents against the U.S. unit.
At Tuesday's close the Zimbabwe dollar was quoted at 11.6300/6400 from 11.6350/6550 on the U.S. dollar and was also firmer against sterling at 18.9300/9500 compared to Monday's 18.9500/9780.
It was at 6.2000/2100 on the mark from 6.2300/2380 but eased slightly on the rand to 2.5000/5100 from 2.4980/5020.
